blocks.content: Ecosystem services are the benefits people obtain from ecosystems, encompassing provisioning, regulating, cultural, and supporting services that sustain human life.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Ecosystem services are the direct and indirect benefits that human beings derive from natural ecological processes.
The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (2005) classified ecosystem services into four major categories: Provisioning, Regulating, Cultural, and Supporting services.
Robert Costanza and his colleagues estimated the average economic value of global ecosystem services to be nearly US$ 33 trillion per year.
Soil formation represents the single largest share of global ecosystem service value, accounting for approximately 50% of total estimated costs.

rows: Direct physical products obtained from healthy ecosystems
Food, fresh water, fuelwood, fiber, and medicinal resources
Benefits obtained from natural control of ecosystem processes
Climate regulation, flood control, disease suppression, and pollination
Underlying processes necessary for the production of all other services
Soil formation, primary production, and nutrient cycling
Non-material benefits that enrich human cultural and spiritual development
Ecotourism, aesthetic inspiration, spiritual fulfillment, and recreation

items: Categorization questions are extremely common: Ensure you correctly classify specific services like pollination (regulating), crop yield (provisioning), and soil formation (supporting).
Costanza's valuation study ($33 trillion annually vs $18 trillion global GNP at the time) is a standard factual question in environment papers.
Identify the breakdown of global ecosystem service costs: Soil formation (~50%), recreation (~10%), nutrient cycling (~10%), and climate regulation (~6%).
